title: Casualty Claims Handler
description:
A renowned National Loss Adjusting Organisation are now seeking an experienced Liability Claims Handler to join their specialist Casualty Liability Team.
- You will handle a variety of specialist Liability claims, predominantly EL & PL and Third-Party Property Damage losses.
- You will manage and be responsible for your own caseload of losses, being part of a dedicated team you will play a vital part of the business by providing an exceptional claims service to key clients.
- Due to growth and expansion this will be an exciting time to join where you will be offered the opportunity to progress and develop long-term.

Key responsibilities:
- Handle predominantly EL & PL claims through to settlement
- Manage your own dedicated caseload of Casualty claims and handling enquiries in relation to policy indemnity, legal liability and quantum
- Liaise with the Insurer, Policyholder and Broker
- Investigate allocated claims, looking at evidence and liaising with all relevant parties and determining liability
- Where appropriate refer to a field adjuster for site investigation to establish how the loss occurred
- Gather all necessary evidence and relevant documentation
- Determine appropriate action for resolution
- Negotiate settlement where appropriate
- Keep up to date with any technical changes within the industry and to your role which may involve participating in training programmes within the company

About you:
- Liability/Casualty Claims handling experience specifically EL & PL (Personal Injury) including Property Damage within the Loss Adjusting, Insurance or Legal Industry
- Experience of handling your caseload of claims through to settlement
- The ability to value an injury loss
- Experience of handling defendant losses
- Excellent communication skills both verbal and written
- Good planning and organisational skills
- Solid IT skills and be able to use multiple in-house systems
- Insurance Industry Qualifications or working towards desirable

Benefits on offer:
- Remote or hybrid depending on location, 35 hours per week Monday to Friday
- Flexible benefits including holiday purchase plan and the opportunity to purchase health cash and BUPA dental plan, flexible working, 5% pension, life assurance 4 x, enhanced maternity, paternity, and adoption pay, discounts with UK retailers, wellbeing hub and many more

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Customer Service Advisor

Red Recruitment is recruiting Customer Service Advisors in Leeds city centre to join our client, an award-winning customer management company that has achieved GOLD awards from both Investors in People and Investors in Customers.

In this role, you will provide telephone support to enforcement agents attending customers properties in relation to outstanding utility debt. You will complete structured fact-finding checks, review account information and ensure the correct legal, regulatory and operational procedures have been followed before any action is taken.

You will help ensure every case is handled fairly, accurately and with appropriate consideration for the customer s individual circumstances.

Benefits and Package for a Customer Service Advisor:
- Salary: £26,227.50 per annum
- Hours: Full-time, Monday to Friday, working hours between 8am and 6pm
- Contract Type: Permanent
- Location: Leeds city centre
- Free parking
- Health and wellbeing programme
- Monthly bonus scheme
- Internal recognition schemes with financial awards
- 33 days annual leave, including bank holidays and your birthday
- Social events, including Summer and Christmas parties
- Full support and training provided
- Career progression opportunities

Key Responsibilities of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Provide telephone and operational support to enforcement agents attending customers properties
- Complete a structured fact-finding process with agents during live property visits
- Review customer accounts, outstanding debt information and previous actions taken
- Check that the relevant legal, regulatory and company procedures have been followed correctly
- Confirm that all required notices, documentation and warrant-related checks have been completed
- Identify factors that could affect how a case should proceed, including vulnerability, affordability concerns or a change of occupier
- Provide guidance to field agents on the appropriate next steps in line with company procedures
- Stop or escalate cases where information is incomplete, procedures have not been followed or additional support is required
- Monitor live cases and provide operational support to help visits progress safely and appropriately
- Escalate complex, sensitive or high-risk cases to specialist teams when required

Key Skills and Experience of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Previous experience in customer service, contact centre, operations support, collections or a regulated environment
- Experience supporting vulnerable customers or handling sensitive situations would be advantageous
- Strong questioning and fact-finding skills, with the confidence to obtain accurate information
- Excellent verbal communication skills and the ability to provide clear guidance over the telephone
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow structured procedures accurately
- Good judgement, with the confidence to challenge, stop or escalate a case when necessary
- Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
- Experience within utilities, debt recovery, revenue protection, financial services or another regulated sector would be beneficial

If you are interested in this position and have the relevant skills and experience required, please apply now!

- Managing the full on-boarding process for new starters, including right to work checks, issuing offers and contracts, completing on-boarding activities and setting up employee records.
- Managing the off-boarding process for leavers and ensuring everything is completed within payroll deadlines.
- Processing changes to terms and conditions, including preparing letters and communicating changes to employees.

- Previous experience within HR administration or HR support.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

- Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage a high-volume workload.
- The confidence to work independently and take ownership of your workload.

title: Internal Sales Administrator
description:
Breedon Group plc is a leading vertically integrated construction materials group in Great Britain, Ireland, and the USA. We're dedicated to providing high-quality materials and services for the construction industry, with a commitment to safety, sustainability, and innovation. Joining Breedon means becoming part of a team that values excellence and is committed to making a positive impact.

Position Overview:
We are currently seeking an Internal Sales Administrator based at our Leeds concrete plant.

You will be a key member of the sales team focused on the sales of construction material products.

Key Responsibilities

You will be responsible for dealing with inbound enquiries from customers, offering sales admin support to Territory Sales Managers and pricing/chasing/winning orders.

To positively represent the Breedon brand, the Internal Sales Representative offers our customers an excellent and professional service.

The key responsibilities of the role are as follows:
- Ensure all phones are answered in a timely manner, and enquiries recorded.
- Raise quotations and price them within the tolerances agreed by the TSM responsible for the area.
- Add relevant notes to enquiries detailing any correspondence with the customer.
- Process order acknowledgments when POs received and confirm via notes on Excalibur.
- Administration of the Cash Sales Process including the recording of the data for the Purchase Ledger Team.
- Generate weekly reports for the Area Sales Manager, reporting key sales data and any significant enquiries.
- Actively seek and identify opportunities to sell additional products and upsell on the initial enquiry received.
- Work pro-actively to identify new or declining customers, sites and opportunities.
- You may on occasion be required to cover other departments.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise
- Focus on the customer relationship - maintain good customer relations and actively build new ones
- Desire to succeed and build on customer base, upselling a range of products to ensure that Breedon succeeds and is the solution of choice for appropriate building projects
- Peruse personal development of our product range
- Effective time management, adhering to administrative policies and procedures
- Attention to detail to ensure sales data produced is accurate

Job Benefits

A tailored, competitive salary
Company Pension Scheme
25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays on top
Share Saver Scheme participation
Company Life Assurance Scheme
Access to our Employee Assistance Programme for health and wellbeing support
Discounts on a wide range of products through our employee benefits platform
Broad learning opportunities and career progression pathways

Diversity Statement:
At Breedon Group, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity is valued. We believe in equality of opportunity for all and encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates.

Join Us:
If you're looking for a role that challenges you, offers progression, and contributes to building better futures, we'd love to hear from you. This position is an opportunity to grow your career within a supportive and dynamic environment at Breedon Group.

Application Process:
Ready to make a meaningful difference? Apply now by submitting your CV and cover letter. We look forward to considering your application and potentially welcoming you to our team.

title: Service Administrator
description:
WSR is recruiting for a Service Administrator for our reputable client in Leeds.

Location: Leeds - Fully office-based, 5 days per week
Salary: £28k per annum
Job Type: Permanent
Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00am 4:30pm

Are you an organised and proactive administrator who enjoys variety and working as part of a busy team? We re looking for a Service Administrator to join a growing service operation in Leeds, providing essential day-to-day support to engineers, customers and the wider service team.

Service Administrator Role Overview:

This is a varied role where no two days are quite the same. You ll be involved in everything from coordinating service calls and engineer schedules through to raising purchase orders, preparing invoices, producing reports and liaising directly with customers. Full training will be provided, making this a great opportunity for someone looking to build their experience within a service, engineering or technical environment.

Service Administrator Key Responsibilities:
- Raising and managing service calls and engineer work orders
- Coordinating engineer diaries and scheduling works with customer sites
- Processing engineer timesheets, reports and daily hours
- Setting up new customers and completing relevant administration
- Raising purchase orders, processing credits and assisting with invoicing
- Reviewing margins and compiling regular service and transaction reports
- Maintaining holiday, sickness, absence and maintenance records
- Monitoring customer KPIs and ensuring scheduled maintenance visits are completed
- Following up on outstanding invoices and liaising with customers as required
- Preparing straightforward customer quotations
- Supporting the wider service team with general day-to-day administration

Service Administrator Skills, Experience & Attributes:

You ll ideally have previous administrative experience, particularly within a service, engineering or technical environment, although this isn t essential as full training will be provided.

You ll also need:
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- The ability to juggle multiple priorities in a busy environment
- Confident written and verbal communication skills
- A friendly, customer-focused approach
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office
- A collaborative approach and willingness to support the wider team
- Basic financial awareness would be useful, although training can be provided
- SAP experience would be advantageous, but isn t essential

Service Administrator Benefits:
- Annual Bonus
- Holidays: 25 days (with increases based on service).
- Health: Private healthcare, digital GP access, and mental health support.
- Enhanced Pay: Generous maternity, paternity, and sick pay.
- Secure Future: Pension plan, income protection, and life assurance (4x salary).
- Employee Rewards: Recognition platform, discounts, Cycle 2 Work scheme, and more!

If you re looking for a varied administration role where you can become an integral part of a busy service team and continue developing your skills, we d love to hear from you.

Please click APPLY NOW , or call the WSR Team at for more info. We appreciate the time and effort invested in your application.

While we strive to respond to all applicants promptly, we kindly ask for your understanding in case of delays. If you do not hear from us within 10 days of submitting your application, please assume that, unfortunately, you have not been successful this time.

We will however keep your CV on file and review your suitability against any other vacancies we may have available.

title: Clerical Officer/Receptionist
description: To provide a high standard of clerical/reception service to patients and the department, adhering to departmental guidelines and policies. The post holder will receive and check documentation, reports, patient information, processing appropriately, within departmental guidelines, including entering information on to the appropriate IT system, and retrieve information as and when required. To process patient and other documentation. To be the first point of contact for patients and other visitors to the department. To provide an administrative/clerical service to the department/team. To support the delivery of a high standard of service to patients, staff and Trust departments. For questions about this job, contact: Name: Madison Calvert Position: Supervisor Email: madisoncalvert@nhs.net Shortlisting Date: 24-09-2026 Interview Date: 30-09-2026 Why you should join our Team Come and join our diverse workforce and become part of The Leeds Way sharing our vision and values. Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is one of the largest acute health providers in the UK and based in one of the fastest growing and vibrant cities in the north. At Leeds Dental Hospital we aim to be a fair, inclusive and supportive CSU with positive caring teams who are champions of the Leeds Way values. Our Trust values of being kind, open and honest, responsible and one team, make us different from other Trusts and we see this as a strength, as well as a responsibility. We offer employees a range of value propositions such as job security, possible flexible working, pension scheme, cycle to work scheme, option to purchase additional annual leave, salary sacrifice scheme + more What you will bring to the role The candidate will bring a professional, organised and positive approach to the role, with the ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of a team. They have strong interpersonal and communication skills, enabling them to communicate clearly and respectfully with patients, colleagues and stakeholders. They are able to multitask and prioritise effectively in a busy environment, while managing their workload efficiently and working within agreed departmental guidelines. They are also willing to undertake any training required, including learning a range of Patient Administration and other systems, demonstrating a commitment to developing their skills and supporting the needs of the service. They have been developed by our staff and set out what they see as important to how we work. title: Medical Administrator
description: Oakwood Lane Medical Practice is delighted to offer an opportunity for a dedicated Medical Administrator to join our friendly, forward thinking team. We care for a diverse population of over 14,000 patients and pride ourselves on delivering high quality, patient centred healthcare. We are looking for an enthusiastic, organised and proactive administrator who is passionate about supporting excellent patient care. You will play a key role in ensuring patients receive the right care at the right time, contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the practice. Join us and become part of a supportive, inclusive and dynamic team committed to delivering outstanding healthcare. Document and Record Management Process, scan and code incoming clinical correspondence. Assign documents to the correct clinician or administrative team promptly and accurately. Identify and escalate urgent or clinically significant information. Liaise with clinicians to clarify documentation queries and ensure appropriate action. Maintain accurate patient records using workflow systems. Process incoming and outgoing patient records. Referral Administration Complete and submit patient referrals to specialists and external providers, ensuring all documentation is accurate and complete. Take ownership of referrals from initiation to completion, including monitoring rejections and responses. Provide clear information to patients regarding referral pathways and progress. Ensure all referral communications are documented and filed appropriately. Insurance and Third Party Requests Manage insurance forms, medical reports and third party documentation with accuracy and compliance. Support patients and staff with queries relating to access to medical records and permissions. General Administrative Support Provide flexible administrative cover across departments as required. Support statutory and contractual practice obligations. Assist with ad-hoc administrative tasks to ensure smooth day to day operations. Work collaboratively with colleagues and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives. Process, scan and code incoming clinical correspondence including hospital letters, discharge summaries, ambulance notifications and out of hours reports. Review correspondence and ensure documents are attached to the correct patient record. Code or free text clinical information on to the patient record. Assign documents to the appropriate clinician or administrative team promptly and accurately. Identify urgent, abnormal or clinically significant information and escalate in accordance with practice procedures. Liaise with clinical staff to clarify documentation queries and ensure appropriate actions are completed. Maintain accurate patient records using practice workflow and clinical systems. Process incoming and outgoing patient records in accordance with NHS and practice procedures, ensuring records are transferred, received and managed accurately and securely. Monitor workflow queues to ensure correspondence is processed within agreed timescales. Deal with queries relating to correspondence management and document processing. Complete and submit referrals to secondary care, community services and external providers, ensuring all supporting documentation is accurate and complete. Take ownership of referrals from initiation through to completion. Monitor referral progress, including rejected referrals, requests for further information and provider responses. Liaise with clinicians to obtain information required to support referrals. Provide patients with information regarding referral pathways, appointments and progress where appropriate. Ensure all referral activity, communications and outcomes are accurately documented and filed within the patient record. Support the practice in achieving referral processing targets and standards. Manage insurance reports, medical reports and third-party documentation requests in accordance with practice procedures and relevant legislation. Ensure documentation is completed accurately and within agreed timescales. Support patients and staff with queries relating to access to medical records, consent and permissions. Maintain accurate records of requests, actions and outcomes. Escalate complex or sensitive requests to the appropriate manager or clinician. Statutory and Contractual Support Support the management of requests for information, reports and returns relating to the practice's statutory and contractual obligations. Assist with administrative processes required to support regulatory, contractual and operational requirements. Undertake any other reasonable duties requested by the management team in support of the practice's business operations.

title: Administrator
description: THE PHARMACIST NETWORK Administrator Job Description Reports to: Business Operations Coordinator Direct reports: None Location: Newcastle, Hybrid Working pattern: Full-time, Monday-Friday 9am-5pm Salary: £26,000 £27,000 The Administrator keeps the day-to-day administration of the TPN central team running. It is a broad, hands-on support role: managing shared inboxes and correspondence, maintaining accurate records across TPN's systems, preparing documentation, and coordinating the routine processes that keep a busy operations function moving. The role suits someone organised and IT literate who is comfortable owning routine work end to end, spotting when something has been missed, and keeping records clean without being chased. Key accountabilities: Manage TPN's shared administrative inboxes triaging enquiries, responding to routine correspondence, and routing what needs a specialist to the right person. Maintain accurate, current records across TPN's systems and shared drives data entry, file management, version control, and routine housekeeping. Prepare and format documents, templates, reports, and correspondence to a consistent standard. Support the compliance administration around TPN's workforce collating and filing documentation, tracking what is outstanding, and flagging gaps for the responsible manager. Coordinate meetings and diary logistics scheduling, room and video setup, circulating papers, and taking and distributing notes where required. Provide administrative support to the wider central team on projects and recurring operational tasks. Handle sensitive and confidential information in line with GDPR and TPN's data handling requirements. Contribute to improving administrative processes surfacing what is slow, duplicated, or manual, and helping tidy it up. Essential experience: Prior administrative experience in an office, operations, or business support setting Experience maintaining records or databases with a high standard of accuracy Experience managing a shared inbox or handling routine correspondence on behalf of a team Desirable: Healthcare, primary care, pharmacy, or NHS-adjacent experience Experience supporting a compliance, HR, or recruitment administration process Familiarity with CRM, ATS, or workflow systems (TPN is moving onto the Zoho ecosystem) Experience working in a hybrid team across multiple sites

title: Patient Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, efficient and friendly patient administrator for this newly designed post. The postholder will be responsible for clearing the task list in SystmOne, ringing and booking patients in for reviews and tests, and responding to queries. They will work alongside the care navigation team and clinical teams to help deliver an excellent standard of care for our patients. The post is 24-28 hours per week, with days and hours to suit the successful candidate. A GP practice is a fast-paced, teamworking environment, requiring the ability to work under pressure and to absorb regular changes. Excellent attention to detail and high levels of accuracy are required to ensure an excellent and safe service for our patients. Candidates who recently applied for the temporary admin/secretarial post are welcome to apply for this post. Responsible for clearing the admin team task list throughout the week, which will include: Contacting patients to arrange their healthcare reviews, blood tests, etc. either by phone, Anima (eConsultation/SMS system), email or letter. Dealing with patients in a caring, respectful and polite manner. Ensuring patients are kept up to date with the progress of any routine issue they may have raised, e.g. an update on their care pathway, prescription query, etc. Arranging home blood pressure monitoring. Ensuring patient information is passed onto the correct staff member in a timely manner and recorded clearly on the patient record. Liaising with clinical colleagues and managerial staff to ensure the most efficient use of the appointment system. The Patient Administrator is primarily responsible for clearing the admin task list in SystmOne Workflow and booking patients in for their reviews and/or tests in an organised and efficient manner. This post involves a lot of patient contact and so the postholder will be friendly, polite, caring and professional. Primary responsibilities: Clearing the admin teams task list in SystmOne workflow. Contacting patients to organise healthcare reviews and tests, in a kind and courteous manner. Putting patients at ease and providing clear, concise information. Making clear and concise notes of patient interactions and ensuring these are documented accurately in the SystmOne clinical software tool. Dealing appropriately with instructions and queries from clinicians and outside agencies. Maintaining strict confidentiality in relation to all issues concerned within requirements of the Data Protection Act 1984, Information Governance and Caldicott Principles. Remaining up to date with all statutory and mandatory training. Additional (as appropriate) Dealing with patient requests received via the online consult system. Responding to email requests received, as appropriate. Supporting the pharmacy team with patient prescription requests.
